title: Feature Waves and Go-to-Market Playbook — Q3 2026
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:

This document outlines the Feature Waves for Q3 2026 and a prescriptive Go-to-Market (GTM) playbook for launching the next set of Redwood Inference product capabilities. It covers product scope, measurable success criteria, rollout phases, pricing/packaging impacts, monitoring and SLO targets, launch gating, and ownership.

Context and intent:
- Objective: Deliver three prioritized feature waves that increase hosted API ARR, improve Dedicated utilization, and accelerate Private deployment adoption for regulated accounts.
- Timebox: Q3 2026 (planned cadence: Wave A launch week of 2026-07-12).
- Audience: Product, Growth, Engineering, SRE, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success.

Goals & Success Metrics:
- Host API Revenue (net-new): +18% month-over-month across Q3 driven by Wave A/B feature adoption.
- Dedicated Capacity Utilization: increase committed utilization from 62% -> 78% by 2026-09-30.
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) for customers on Private: reduce median onboarding time from 21 days -> 10 days.
- Quality guardrail: fewer than 0.5% increase in generation error-rate within 30 days post-launch per model route.

Target customers and personas:
- PLG engineers (small/medium apps) — prioritize Wave A low-friction features and SDKs.
- Platform & Security buyers (enterprise) — prioritize Wave C private deployment and compliance packaging.
- Embedded AI product teams — prioritize Wave B cost/perf controls and model variants.

Feature Waves (high level):

| Wave | Primary Features (owner) | Primary KPI | Target SLO / Perf Target | Pricing impact |
|------|-------------------------|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|
| Wave A (Q3 start) | SDK streaming primitives + standardized prompt templates (owner: DX team) | # API calls with streaming >= 2x baseline | 95th p95 latency <= 450ms (1k tokens) | Minor: no pricing change; feature flag gating |
| Wave B (mid-Q3) | Cost-aware batching & adaptive quantization advisory (owner: Optimize team) | Per-token cost reduction observed in A/B test >= 12% | 99% of requests below cost-SLO with <2% latency tail regressions | Introduce optional per-route optimization add-on (beta pricing) |
| Wave C (late-Q3) | Private deployment quickstart + certified compliance bundle (owner: Private deployments team) | # Private pilots -> paid conversions within 90 days >= 40% | On-prem bootstrap time <= 48 hours for certified configs | New enterprise packaging; platform fee + deployment license (see Pricing section) |

(Notes: Table rendered above as ASCII for Confluence; owners are team leads.)

Rollout plan (detailed):
1) Pre-launch (T-6 to T-2 weeks)
   - Complete product-signoff checklist (owners signoff: PM, Eng, SRE, Security).
   - Create feature flags: ff.streaming_v2, ff.adaptive_batch_v1, ff.private_quickstart_v1.
   - Prepare SDK changelog and migration guide (DX).
   - Set up A/B experiment: sampling rule (1% control, 49% baseline, 50% variant) for Wave B cost experiment.
2) Limited rollout (T-2 to T+2 weeks)
   - Enable for internal + partner accounts, Solutions Engineering-run pilots.
   - Monitor: latency_p95_by_route, error_rate_by_route, cost_per_1k_tokens.
   - Weekly quality reviews; rollback threshold: error_rate increase > 0.8% absolute or latency_p95 regress > 30% relative.
3) Open rollout (T+2 to T+8 weeks)
   - Gradual ramp to 100% for hosted customers per routing policy; provide migration CLI (redwood migrate-streams).
   - Announce public docs + quickstart templates; launch self-serve opt-in for optimization add-on.
4) Enterprise enablement (post T+8 weeks)
   - Dedicated & Private sales motions: package templates, pricing worksheets, compliance evidence bundles.
   - Offer day-2 runbook and 90-day SLA uplift conversations (SRE & Sales).

Release gating & launch criteria:
- Blocking criteria (must be green before open rollout):
  - Stability: <0.2% production error-rate attributable to feature on internal canary fleet for 7 consecutive days.
  - Performance: p95 latency within 10% of baseline for 99% of routes (where baseline is previous quarter median).
  - Security & compliance: Customer-data-handling review completed and ATO checklist signed by Security.
  - Documentation: SDK migration guide, quickstarts, sample prompts, and runbook published.

Pricing & packaging considerations (product notes):
- Wave A: No price change; included in hosted API tier. Market message focuses on DX/velocity benefits.
- Wave B: Introduce a new optional "Optimize Add-on" priced as a % discount on per-token billing when the system applies adaptive quantization/batching. Initial beta pricing: 8% of token spend as monthly surcharge that guarantees >=10% realized cost reduction under benchmarked workloads.
- Wave C: Enterprise Private package has two components: platform license (one-time onboarding fee + monthly platform fee) and deployment license (per-node or per-GPU). Suggested list: onboarding $25k, platform $5k/month, node license $2k/month (negotiable). Include standard SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) mapped to response times and retention.

Sales enablement and playbook snippets:
- Solutions Engineering (SE) checklist for demos:
  - Demo 1 (DX-focused): show streaming + prompt templates; demo script: 10–12 steps with prepopulated prompts.
  - Demo 2 (Optimize-focused): run live cost comparison with and without adaptive batching using benchmark dataset (privacy-safe).
  - Demo 3 (Private-focused): show quickstart deployment on a sandbox VPC with KMS integration.
- Customer objection handling:
  - "Will these features increase costs?" -> Walk through Optimize add-on model: surcharge only when system applies optimizations; show expected cost delta and rollback option.
  - "How do we validate accuracy regressions?" -> Point to regression harness and quality guardrails (prompt sets + golden outputs).

Monitoring & Observability changes:
- Dashboards to create/update:
  - "Wave A - Streaming adoption" (owner: DX) — metrics: streaming_success_rate, stream_connect_latency, average_stream_tokens.
  - "Wave B - Cost optimization" (owner: Optimize) — metrics: realized_cost_saved_pct, batching_rate, quantization_failures.
  - "Wave C - Private onboarding" (owner: Private deployments) — metrics: bootstrap_time_median, infra_errors_per_bootstrap, compliance_check_pass_rate.
- Alerts & SLOs:
  - streaming_success_rate < 99% for 5m -> pager (severity P2) to DX oncall.
  - realized_cost_saved_pct < 6% for 1h during beta -> notify Optimize PM and SRE (investigate parameter tuning).
  - bootstrap_time_median > 72 hours -> SRE ticket automation and SE outreach.

Data & experiment plan (Wave B cost experiment):
- Hypothesis: Adaptive batching + quantization advisory reduces observable per-token spend by >=12% without user-visible quality regressions.
- Metric definitions: cost_per_1k_tokens = (infrastructure_costs_allocated / tokens_generated) * 1000; quality_regression = BLEU/ROUGE-based delta + manual spot checks on 500 prompt pairs.
- Experiment duration: 28 days with daily reporting. Success threshold: >=12% median cost reduction and <=0.5% regression signal in quality harness.

Dependencies and Risks:
- Dependency: kernel-level quantization support must ship from runtime team by 2026-06-15 for Wave B to meet schedule.
- Risk: performance regressions when applying heavy adaptive batching for small (<64 token) requests. Mitigation: per-route sampling and fallback.
- Risk: enterprise purchase cycles may delay Wave C revenue realization. Mitigation: early pilot discounts + documented onboarding SLAs.

Ownership, milestones, and timeline:
- PM leads: Priya Nair (Wave planning), Jordan Blake (Wave B PM), Sofia Martinez (Wave C PM).
- Engineering owners: DX (SDKs), Optimize (cost tools), Private deployments (onboarding).
- Key milestones:
  - 2026-05-15: Feature design freeze for Wave A.
  - 2026-06-15: Runtime quantization kernel availability.
  - 2026-07-12: Wave A limited rollout (partner pilots).
  - 2026-08-02: Wave B experiment starts.
  - 2026-09-20: Wave C enterprise pilot cohort onboarded.

Appendix A — API surface & CLI changes (examples):
- SDK: new method StreamResponse.stream_with_progress(prompt, on_chunk_callback) — see examples in DX quickstart.
- CLI: redwood optimize analyze --route <route_id> --profile perf -> outputs suggested batch/quantization profile JSON.

Appendix B — Templates and artifacts to publish:
- Migration guide: "Streaming v1 -> v2" (DX).
- Experiment dashboard: "cost-optimization-a-b" (Optimize).
- Sales pricing worksheet + negotiation playbook (Go-to-market).
